The exception is a runtime exception, so it does not need to be declared or caught. The intent is to fail fast and signal a programming error—the caller should have ensured it is on the correct thread before invoking the operation. The programmer likely expects this exception to propagate up to crash the program or be caught by a top-level exception handler, not to be caught and handled locally, as recovery is not feasible without changing the threading context.
